craft_evidence.owned: no evidence: no factory named on site; our-story timeline names Wilton and Farmington, Maine factories (1876) but nothing current; site operated by ALDO (Montreal) under licence, IP owned by G.H. Bass IPCo LLC (G-III)
craft_evidence.makers: no: 0 of 12 sampled men's PDPs name a maker
craft_evidence.mills: no: no tannery or leather supplier named (PDP Materials block reads Material: Leather / Lining / Insole / Sole only)
craft_evidence.madein: 0 of 12 sampled men's PDPs (loafers, boots, boat shoe, Chelsea) state a country of origin; feed body_html states none on 194 footwear products
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: George H. Bass begins shoemaking 9 March 1876, Wilton, Maine; factory moved to Wilson Stream, Farmington, Maine 1876; Weejuns introduced 1936
craft_evidence.process: partial: craftsmanship page and Larson PDP describe handsewn tubular moccasin (four-part pattern), two-needle beefroll, Blake-stitched resoleable leather outsole, antiquing of whiskey/wine colourways; no place or maker attached
craft_evidence.reasoning: G.H.BASS documents how a Weejun is made (handsewn moccasin, beefroll, Blake-stitched resoleable sole) and dates its founding to Wilton, Maine in 1876, but names no current factory, maker or tannery, and none of 12 sampled product pages states a country of origin. The Maine factories are history, not present making; the brand is now an IP licence operated by ALDO. Process without a place or maker sits at 2, not 3.
